title: Pointer-addressed document patches: 7 ops, up-front validation, atomicity, JSON equality and diff

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 1: "/" is [""], "/a//b" is ["a", "", "b"]; ~1 -> / and ~0 -> ~ decoded left to right in a single pass ("/~01" is ["~1"]).
Rule 1: a ~ not followed by 0/1, non-strings and strings not starting with / raise invalid-pointer with index None and pointer = the argument.
Rule 2: format_pointer is the exact inverse: [] -> ""; ~ -> ~0, / -> ~1, each token prefixed with /.
Rule 3: list tokens must be 0 or [1-9][0-9]*; -, 01, +1, 1.0, ' 1' -> invalid-index; index >= len -> path-not-found; "01" and "-" are ordinary dict keys. Rule 4: index None, pointer = argument.
Rule 3: traversal through any scalar or a missing key -> path-not-found; rule 1/4: "" is the whole document.
Rule 5: a bool equals only a bool (True != 1, False != 0), None only None, numbers numerically (1 == 1.0), recursively.
Rule 5: lists order matters, dicts same key set (key order irrelevant), strings by value.
Rule 11: parent dict -> set the key, replacing an existing value; rule 3: "01" is an ordinary key.
Rule 11: '-' appends; 0 <= i <= len inserts before i; i > len -> path-not-found; non-index token -> invalid-index.
Rule 11: add with path "" replaces the whole document.
Rule 11: parent located with rule 3 (missing -> path-not-found, '-' in the middle -> invalid-index); parent scalar -> path-not-found; rule 10 pointer = path.
Rule 7: presence of value is what counts; "value": None is a valid value for add/replace/test.
Rule 12: target must exist (missing -> path-not-found, '-' -> invalid-index), later elements shift left; path "" -> cannot-remove-root.
Rule 13: path "" replaces the whole document; otherwise the target must exist (rule 3).
Rule 14(d): value removed from `from` then added at `path` using add rules on the document after removal ([a,b,c] /l/0 -> /l/2 gives [b,c,a]).
Rule 14(c): from tokens a proper prefix of path tokens -> move-into-self (token-wise: /a/b -> /a/bc allowed, /a -> /a/b not, "" -> non-empty not).
Rule 14(a)/(b): the from location must exist; identical tokens do nothing.
Rule 10/14: failures locating from report pointer = from; add failures after removal report pointer = path.
Rule 14(d) + rule 11: adding at "" after removal replaces the whole document.
Rule 15: a deep copy of the from value is added at path with the add rules; rule 8 sequential ops; rule 9 no sharing.
Rule 15: from must exist (errors report the from pointer); add rules at path (rule 11).
Rule 16: target must exist; value not json_equal -> test-failed (rule 5 equality).
Rule 17: target replaced by target + by; int when both int, otherwise float.
Rule 17: target must exist and be an int/float that is not a bool, else type-mismatch.
Rule 7: inc must have a `by` that is int or float but not bool, else invalid-op.
Rule 7: the whole patch is validated structurally before any operation is applied; invalid path -> invalid-pointer with pointer = that path.
Rule 7: if several operations are structurally invalid, the one with the lowest index is reported.
Rule 7: op must be one of the seven names; path present and a string; add/replace/test need value; move/copy need a string from.
Rule 7: from must be a valid pointer, else invalid-pointer with pointer = that from.
Rule 7: unknown extra members are ignored.
Rule 6: patch must be a list (index None) of dicts (element index).
Rule 8: on failure PatchError with the failing op index and nothing is changed; apply_patch never mutates document.
Rules 8/9: never mutates document or patch; the result shares no mutable containers with the input or the patch.
Rule 8: operations are applied in order; each sees the result of the previous ones.
Rule 23: DocumentStore.patch leaves the stored document and revision unchanged when the patch fails (relies on rule 8).
Rule 20: json_equal documents -> [] (diff(1, 1.0) is []); diff(True, 1) is not; rule 21 root replace.
Rule 21: differing JSON types (int/float both number) or unequal scalars -> a single replace of that location.
Rule 22: removes for source-only keys (ascending), then recursive diffs of common keys (ascending), then adds for target-only keys (ascending); rule 19 members.
Rule 19: keys containing / or ~ and the empty key are escaped per rule 2; rule 22 ordering; rule 18 round trip.
Rule 18: apply_patch(source, diff(source, target)) is json_equal to target (arrays of differing lengths).
Rules 18-20: round trip for arbitrary documents, diff does not mutate its arguments, only add/remove/replace with exactly op/path(/value) members, equal documents give [].
Rule 19: values in emitted operations are deep copies.
